name: Evergreen and Semi-Liquid Vehicles
summary: Interval funds, non-traded and perpetual BDCs, tender-offer funds, NAV REITs and evergreen PE sold to wealth and 401(k) channels: illiquid assets inside a vehicle that promises periodic liquidity, typically 5% of shares a quarter, with proration, queues or gates above the cap. The 2026 private-credit redemption stress (OBDC II ended redemptions; Q2 2026 first aggregate net outflow, $10.7B unmet; requests of about 22% and 40% at two Blue Owl vehicles) is the case study: stale marks plus a 5% gate plus thin cash produced gating, rising leverage and deferred payments. The spine is a liquidity coverage ratio stressed for four consecutive quarters at the cap without new inflows; mark-lag and cross-BDC mark tests; PIK and amend-and-extend tracking; software exposure; leverage-redemption feedback; distribution source; and who decides the gate. Non-traded REIT coverage in the bible is thin (appraisal-based marks only).
one_check: Compute the liquidity coverage ratio for four consecutive quarters of maximum redemptions, using marks rolled forward for public-market moves; if coverage depends on new inflows or new borrowing, the vehicle is only as liquid as its next sales quarter.

subtypes.name: Interval fund
subtypes.description: Registered closed-end fund making periodic repurchase offers under a fundamental policy.

subtypes.name: Non-traded / perpetual BDC
subtypes.description: Business development company sold continuously; discretionary repurchases; 90% income distribution requirement.

subtypes.name: Tender-offer fund
subtypes.description: Fund offering discretionary periodic tender offers.

subtypes.name: Non-traded / NAV REIT
subtypes.description: Perpetual REIT with appraisal-based NAV and limited repurchases (thin bible coverage).

intake_questions.question: Is the vehicle an interval fund, non-traded BDC, tender-offer fund or non-traded/NAV REIT?
What is the repurchase cap and frequency, and are repurchases mandatory or discretionary?
intake_questions.why: Drives the LCR denominator and gate risk.

intake_questions.question: Has the vehicle ever prorated, queued or gated requests?
intake_questions.why: Gating history is the leading run signal.

intake_questions.question: What share of the book is software or a single sector?
Which distribution channels and wealth platforms hold the shares?
Does the vehicle use credit facilities, sub lines or NAV facilities, and may they fund redemptions?
Is the product offered through a tokenized wrapper?

requests.request: Prospectus or PPM and charter of the vehicle.
requests.format: Current filed prospectus or PPM with all supplements; charter and bylaws.
requests.why: Defines the repurchase promise, fees, leverage and valuation regime.
requests.pass: Current documents received and consistent with marketing.
requests.fail: Marketing promises liquidity the documents do not.
requests.verify: Pull filed versions from SEC EDGAR where registered.

requests.request: Repurchase or tender-offer policy (for interval funds, the fundamental repurchase policy), including cap, frequency, proration and carry-forward rules.
requests.why: Vehicle promises periodic liquidity on illiquid assets, typically 5% of shares per quarter, and prorates, queues or gates above the cap.
requests.pass: Policy states cap, proration and whether unmet requests carry forward.
requests.fail: Policy vague on cap, proration or carry-forward.
requests.verify: Compare with prospectus and board resolutions.

requests.request: Redemption history by quarter since launch: requests, cap, amount paid, prorated, queued, carried forward, and the 'repurchases payable' balance.
requests.why: Gating history and growing queues are the leading signal of a run (Q2 2026: $10.7B of requests unmet).
requests.pass: Requests below the cap in every quarter, or excess requests paid in full; no growing queue; repurchases payable not rising.
requests.fail: Proration, queues or rising repurchases payable.
requests.verify: Obtain directly from the transfer agent.

requests.request: Flow history: subscriptions and redemptions by month or quarter since launch.
requests.why: Q2 2026 was the sector's first aggregate net outflow ($7.1B repurchases vs $3.8B inflows).
requests.pass: Net inflows not required to meet repurchases.
requests.fail: Repurchases exceed inflows with coverage dependent on new money.

requests.request: Schedule of investments with current marks, cost, maturity and rating for every position.
requests.format: Latest filed schedule (10-Q/10-K/N-CSR) or administrator report.
requests.why: Needed for mark-lag, cross-BDC and concentration tests.
requests.pass: Complete schedule tied to NAV.

requests.request: Full fee schedule: base fee, incentive fees on income and on gains, distribution and servicing fees, acquired-fund fee layers.
requests.format: Prospectus fee table plus underlying-fund fees.
requests.why: All-in fee load must be compared with a levered small-value index; asset-based fees on growing NAV reward inflows.
requests.pass: All-in load disclosed and justified against benchmark.
requests.verify: Recompute total expense ratio from filings.

requests.request: Distribution policy and the source of each of the last eight distributions (income, gains, return of capital, borrowing).
requests.format: Section 19a notices or equivalent, tied to NII.
requests.why: GPB and Heller paid fixed distributions from new money; distributions above NII are not earned.
requests.pass: Distributions covered by NII and realized gains; source disclosed for each.
requests.fail: Fixed distribution rate above NII; distributions funded by borrowing or new money.

requests.request: Investor concentration and distribution channel: share of NAV by wealth platform, adviser network and largest holders.
requests.why: Wealth platforms move together (Blue Owl Q2 2026 requests of about 22% and about 40% of shares).
requests.pass: No platform above a level the LCR could absorb if it redeemed at once.
requests.fail: One platform could exhaust several quarters of capacity.

requests.request: Annual deployment target against the size of the target market.
requests.why: Largest perpetual private-credit fund must deploy about $43B a year, over a quarter of US direct lending.
requests.pass: Deployment a small share of market.
requests.fail: Deployment a material share of market.
requests.verify: Compare with independent market-size estimates (present all; do not average).

requests.request: Gate, suspension and in-kind redemption provisions, and who decides each repurchase and gate.
requests.why: Managers delay using suspensions until late; vague gate provisions are a red flag.
requests.pass: Named decision-maker (independent board), objective criteria, and stated procedure.

requests.request: Treatment of unmet requests: carry forward, resubmission required, or lost.
requests.why: Carry-forward builds a queue that works like debt.
requests.pass: Treatment stated; queued amounts reported.

requests.request: Leverage limits and asset-coverage requirement, and current asset coverage.
requests.why: Leverage-redemption feedback loop.
requests.pass: Asset coverage comfortably above the regulatory or stated minimum after a two-quarter stress.

requests.request: Manager compensation basis: asset-based fees, income incentive fees, and any inflow-linked pay.
requests.why: Manager pay driven by inflows is a red flag.
requests.pass: Material share of pay tied to total return net of losses.
requests.fail: Pay driven by NAV growth and inflows.

requests.request: Fund counsel's memo on the legal basis of the structure (Investment Company Act rules for interval funds and BDCs, REIT status) and the enforceability of repurchase terms.
requests.why: Legal basis of each structure was not sourced in the bible (GAP); confirm with fund counsel.
requests.pass: Memo confirms discretion versus obligation for each repurchase.

requests.request: Liquidity-source schedule: cash, NII run rate and retention, contractual maturities by quarter, committed undrawn facilities usable for repurchases and their covenants.
requests.why: Cash about 5.5% of TNA covers roughly one quarter of full 5% repurchases; NII about 2.5% a quarter is mostly distributed; maturities under 0.5% a quarter.
requests.pass: All sources quantified with maturities by quarter.
requests.verify: Tie to filed financials and lender statements.

requests.request: Liquidity coverage ratio for the current quarter: (cash + retained NII + contractual maturities + committed undrawn facilities usable for repurchases) / maximum repurchase obligation at the cap.
requests.why: The core test for semi-liquid vehicles.
requests.pass: LCR >= 1.0x at the cap, with coverage excluding facilities also reported.
requests.fail: LCR below 1.0x, or coverage relies on facilities alone.

requests.request: LCR stress for four consecutive quarters of maximum (5%) repurchases with no new inflows and marks rolled forward for public-market moves.
requests.why: THE ONE CHECK: if coverage depends on new inflows or new borrowing, the vehicle is only as liquid as its next sales quarter.
requests.pass: LCR >= 1.0x in each of four quarters without new inflows or new borrowing.
requests.fail: Coverage needs inflows, new borrowing, fire sales or the gate.

requests.request: Look-through of 'cash' and 'cash equivalents': money-market, 'cash management' and pooled cash holdings, with a 6- to 24-month gate scenario on each.
requests.why: Reserve Primary Fund gated for years; investors got about 50 cents in six weeks, 99 cents after two years.
requests.pass: Cash held in instruments that do not gate; LCR holds with pooled cash gated.
requests.fail: Liquidity depends on a pooled vehicle that can gate.

requests.request: Repurchases payable and deferred redemption payments, treated as debt in leverage and LCR.
requests.why: Repurchases payable work like trade credit owed to exiting investors.
requests.pass: Small and not rising; included as debt.

requests.request: Valuation policy and NAV strike process: frequency, who marks, and approval chain.
requests.why: Stale NAV gives redeeming investors a first-mover advantage at remaining holders' expense.
requests.pass: Independent valuation of Level 3 assets each strike; documented approval.

requests.request: Independent valuation agent's engagement letter and reports for the last 8 quarters.
requests.why: IMF recommends mandatory independent external valuations; SQN claimed independence falsely.
requests.pass: Agent covers the majority of Level 3 assets and confirms on a call.
requests.fail: No agent or agent covers a small sample only.

requests.request: Mark-to-market lag analysis: NAV and loan marks against comparable public benchmarks (B-rated leveraged loans, public BDCs, listed REITs) around recent shocks.
requests.why: BDC loan marks lag B-rated leveraged loans; price and NAV take at least four quarters to converge after a shock.
requests.pass: Marks track public comparables within one quarter.
requests.fail: Smooth NAV while comparable public credit or equity fell.

requests.request: Comparison of the manager's mark on each loan with the same loan's mark in other BDCs' schedules of investments.
requests.why: BDC filings are one of the few public windows (loans held by private-credit BDCs rose from 1,395 to 20,182, 2010-2022).
requests.pass: Marks at or below peer marks on shared loans.

requests.request: Smoothness test: NAV volatility against the stated strategy and public comparables.
requests.why: Appraisal-based marks smooth volatility; smoothness relative to strategy is also a Ponzi tell.
requests.pass: Volatility consistent with comparables after desmoothing.

requests.request: NAV REIT appraisal process: appraiser identity and independence, frequency, and property appraisals against recent transactions.
requests.why: Appraisal-based marks lag; real estate LP interests traded at 68% of NAV in H1 2026.
requests.pass: Independent appraisers; marks consistent with transactions.

requests.request: PIK income as % of total investment income by quarter since 2019.
requests.why: PIK share of BDC interest income has doubled since 2019.
requests.pass: PIK share stable or falling and below peer median.

requests.request: Amend-and-extend and maturity-extension log by loan for the last 8 quarters.
requests.why: Private lenders can forbear indefinitely, creating zombie borrowers.
requests.pass: Few amendments, each with credit rationale.

requests.request: Sector exposure with software share, and a downside-ARR debt test for software borrowers (AI seat compression and price pressure).
requests.format: Sector table and our ARR stress.
requests.why: About one-fifth of loans in semi-liquid private credit funds are to software firms; 2026 'software crisis'.
requests.pass: Software exposure tested on downside ARR, not ARR multiples; debt serviceable.
requests.fail: Large software concentration underwritten on ARR multiples.

requests.request: Borrower concentration and sponsor-affiliated borrowers.
requests.why: Concentration and conflicts.
requests.pass: No single borrower above stated limit; affiliated loans disclosed.

requests.request: Definition of any default or loss rate quoted in marketing (covenant defaults, payment defaults or realized losses).
requests.why: Proskauer counts covenant defaults; Cliffwater realized losses; agencies payment defaults.
requests.pass: Definition stated and comparable.

requests.request: Look-through of every holding labelled 'alternative assets', 'direct lending' or 'multi-strategy income' to underlying loans.
requests.why: Labels can hide private-loan exposure.
requests.pass: Full look-through.

requests.request: Leverage history by quarter against net flows.
requests.why: Net debt rises 0.38 pp of TNA per 1-point increase in net outflows.
requests.pass: Leverage not rising as flows turn negative.

requests.request: Every credit facility, sub line and NAV facility agreement, with covenants and margin-call triggers, and a statement of whether any is used to meet redemptions.
requests.why: Covenants can force sales; facilities used for redemptions are a red flag.
requests.pass: No facility used to fund redemptions; covenants survive the four-quarter stress.
requests.fail: Facilities fund redemptions or covenants trip in stress.

requests.request: Investor-level (dollar-weighted) returns against fund TWR.
requests.why: Investors in hot vehicles buy near the top.
requests.pass: Gap small and explained.

requests.request: Cash-flow reconciliation showing whether new subscriptions fund redemptions or distributions.
requests.why: Ponzi-like dynamics under stress (GPB).
requests.pass: Redemptions and distributions funded by portfolio cash and income.
requests.fail: New money funds old redemptions or distributions.

requests.request: Distribution coverage: distribution rate versus NII per share over 8 quarters.
requests.why: A fixed distribution rate above NII is a red flag.
requests.pass: NII covers distributions.

requests.request: All-in fee load compared with a levered small-value index.
requests.why: Retail access keeps higher fees.
requests.pass: Net return after all fees exceeds the benchmark.

requests.request: Sponsor support history: insider purchases, fee waivers and support agreements.
requests.why: Sponsor support is discretionary and may not scale.
requests.pass: LCR passes without sponsor support.

requests.request: Board minutes for every repurchase and gating decision.
requests.why: Who decides and on what basis.
requests.pass: Independent directors decided with documented analysis.

requests.request: Secondary-market liquidity of the loan book: share unrated and holder breadth.
requests.why: About 80% unrated; fewer than 20% held by 10+ fund families.
requests.pass: Material share tradable.

requests.request: For tokenized wrappers: token trading speed against the speed at which the underlying can honor redemptions.
requests.why: A tokenized claim that trades faster than the asset can redeem invites a run.
requests.pass: Token redemption matched to underlying.

requests.request: Direct confirmation from the independent valuation agent of scope and positions valued.
requests.why: Claimed independence.
requests.pass: Confirms.

requests.request: Direct confirmation from the administrator and transfer agent of the redemption queue, requests and payments.
requests.why: Queue misreported.
requests.pass: Matches manager data.

requests.request: Auditor confirmation (Big 4 or equivalent) and latest audit opinion.
requests.why: Auditor quality.
requests.pass: Big 4 or equivalent; unqualified.

requests.request: Credit facility lenders' confirmation of availability, covenants and any forced-sale triggers.
requests.why: Covenants that can force sales.
requests.pass: Availability confirmed.

requests.request: Interview with independent directors on valuation and repurchase decisions.
requests.why: Who decides each repurchase.
requests.pass: Directors independent and engaged.

requests.request: Subscription agreement, share-class confirmation and acknowledgement of repurchase, gate and suspension terms.
requests.why: Investor expectations of liquidity.
requests.pass: Terms acknowledged.

requests.request: Bring-down of the redemption queue and LCR as of the subscription date.
requests.why: Buying into a queue.
requests.pass: No queue; LCR passes.

requests.request: Quarterly redemption report: requests, cap, paid, prorated, queued, carried forward, repurchases payable.
requests.why: Run signal.
requests.pass: No proration or queue.

requests.request: Quarterly LCR update with four-quarter stress.
requests.why: Liquidity erosion.
requests.pass: LCR >= 1.0x for four quarters without inflows.

requests.request: NAV per share each strike with mark-lag commentary versus public comparables.
requests.why: Stale marks.
requests.pass: NAV moves with comparables.

requests.request: Source of each distribution.
requests.why: Distributions from capital or borrowing.
requests.pass: Covered by NII.

requests.request: Quarterly PIK share and amend-and-extend log.
requests.why: Hidden losses.
requests.pass: Stable or falling.

requests.request: Quarterly leverage, asset coverage and facility covenant compliance.
requests.why: Leverage-redemption loop.
requests.pass: Compliant with cushion.

requests.request: Annual audited financial statements.
requests.why: Valuation and liquidity misstatement.
requests.pass: Unqualified, on time, Big 4 or equivalent.

requests.request: Prompt notice of any gate, suspension, proration or in-kind decision with board minutes.
requests.why: Gate used late.
requests.pass: Notice same day; minutes provided.

requests.request: Investor account statements from the transfer agent.
requests.why: Statements only from the manager.
requests.pass: Issued by transfer agent; reconcile.

kill_tests.test: LCR below 1.0x within four consecutive quarters at the cap without new inflows or new borrowing.
Distributions or redemptions funded by new subscriptions (GPB, Heller pattern).
No independent valuation of Level 3 assets; manager alone marks the book.
Redemption history (requests, paid, prorated, queued) refused or not confirmable with the transfer agent.
Fund-level sub line or NAV facility used to meet redemptions with covenants that trip in the stress.

red_flags.flag: Rising 'repurchases payable' or a growing queue.
Leverage rising as flows turn negative.
Smooth NAV while comparable public credit or equity fell.
Marks above the same loan's marks in other BDCs.
Fixed distribution rate exceeding NII; distributions funded by borrowing or new money.
Manager pay driven by inflows; deployment target large against the market.
Gate or suspension provisions that are vague about who decides.
Fund-level sub line or NAV facility used to meet redemptions.
Liquidity buffer held in pooled 'cash management' vehicles that can gate.
Investor concentration in one wealth platform.
Opaque sleeves labelled 'alternative assets' or 'multi-strategy income'.

metrics.acceptable: Private debt funds 54.7%; perpetual BDCs 18.7%; public BDCs 12.4%; MM CLOs 5.9%; private BDCs 5.4%; interval funds 3.0%

metrics.source: KaW; IMF GFSR; Fed FEDS Note

metrics.acceptable: At least four quarters

third_party_reports.provider: Independent valuation agent (IMF recommends mandatory independent external valuations)
Independent directors of the BDC or interval fund board

hard_questions.question: Show the redemption history: requests, paid, prorated, queued, every quarter since launch.
hard_questions.good_answer: A transfer-agent table with no proration or queues, or full disclosure of each.

hard_questions.question: What is your liquidity coverage at the cap for four straight quarters, without new inflows?
hard_questions.good_answer: At least 1.0x each quarter from cash, retained income and maturities.

hard_questions.question: Who values the book, and how do your marks compare with other BDCs' marks on the same loans?
hard_questions.good_answer: An independent agent; marks at or below peers on shared loans.

hard_questions.question: What share of income is PIK, and how many loans were amended or extended in the last year?
hard_questions.good_answer: Low and stable PIK share; few amendments with rationale.

hard_questions.question: What share of the book is software, and what is the downside-ARR test?
hard_questions.good_answer: Disclosed share with debt tested on downside ARR.

hard_questions.question: Where did each of the last eight distributions come from?
hard_questions.good_answer: Net investment income and realized gains, each documented.

hard_questions.question: What facilities can you draw to meet redemptions, and what covenants could force sales?
hard_questions.good_answer: None used for redemptions; covenants survive stress.

hard_questions.question: What are investors' dollar-weighted returns, not the fund's TWR?
hard_questions.good_answer: A calculation from flows with the gap explained.

hard_questions.question: Who decides whether to gate, and what did they decide last time?
hard_questions.good_answer: Independent board, documented criteria and minutes.

failure_cases.check: LCR across consecutive quarters at the cap; redemption queue history.

failure_cases.case: Blue Owl Capital Corp II / Blue Owl Credit Income Corp
failure_cases.what_happened: Redemption requests of about 22% and about 40% of shares against a 5% cap.
failure_cases.check: Investor concentration and channel; flow history.

failure_cases.what_happened: First aggregate net outflow ($7.1B out vs $3.8B in); $10.7B gated; rising fund leverage; deferred payments; Blackstone, BlackRock and Apollo vehicles also above the cap.
failure_cases.check: LCR, mark-lag test, queue history, leverage-redemption loop.

failure_cases.what_happened: AI disruption of SaaS sharply revised software borrowers' default probabilities; about one-fifth of semi-liquid fund loans are to software.
$62.5B fund held $785M of Lehman paper; over $40B of requests in two days; broke the buck and suspended; about 50 cents in six weeks, 99 cents after two years, final 99.1 cents in 2014.
Fixed distributions on illiquid assets paid from new investor capital.
Fixed monthly distributions to about 2,700 mostly retail investors paid from new money and short-term loans.
